subject: Startups
title: Founder Mode vs. Manager Mode
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Founder Mode vs. Manager Mode.

hook.text: Paul Graham described 'founder mode'—hands-on, detail-obsessed, skip-level meetings. It clashes with management theory.

buildup.text: Traditional advice says: 'Hire great people and get out of the way.' But many founders fail when they delegate too soon.

discovery.text: Steve Jobs stayed in founder mode forever—reviewing every product detail.

twist.text: The trap: staying in founder mode too long creates bottlenecks. Everything waits for the founder's approval.

climax.text: The skill is knowing when to switch modes. Early on, founder mode builds the product.

punchline.text: Founder mode starts companies. Manager mode scales them.

quiz.question: What did Paul Graham describe as 'founder mode'?
